physical: In a linear medium the net displacement at any point is the sum of the displacements each wave would produce alone. y = y1 + y2
reflected_formula: y = y1 + y2 (kept as given; y has no frozen partner)
reflected_sentence: It keeps its shape: the net vibration is the sum of what each vibration brings alone, and on the nonphysical side two vibrations do more than add — they culminate, since the book itself has a sum here and the sum crosses whole.
rule_reason: It is an identity in a linear medium; identities keep their shape; no costs named.
interpretation: An identity crosses whole, sum and all, because the book itself writes a sum here. Culminate is the frozen word for what two vibrations do together. Amplitude never finds a partner.
closing: The rule decided alone: an identity with no costs keeps. The trap about sums does not bite because the physical relation itself is a sum. Ch 16's word culminate fits without stretching, which lifts this row above the bare-symbol rows.
